AbstractText.Label: Context
AbstractText.content: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) consists of a small/absent anterior pituitary lobe, interrupted/absent pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary lobe. Mendelian forms of PSIS are detected infrequently (< 5%), and a polygenic etiology has been suggested. GLI2 variants have been reported in a relatively high frequency in PSIS.

AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: To provide further evidence for a non-Mendelian, polygenic etiology of PSIS.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: Exome sequencing (trio approach) in 20 patients with isolated PSIS. In addition to searching for (potentially) pathogenic de novo and biallelic variants, a targeted search was performed in a panel of genes associated with midline brain development (223 genes). For GLI2 variants both (potentially) pathogenic and relatively rare variants (< 5% in the general population) were studied. The frequency of GLI2 variants was compared to a reference population.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: We found 4 new candidate genes for isolated PSIS (DCHS1, ROBO2, CCDC88C, KIF14) and one for syndromic PSIS (KAT6A). Eleven GLI2 variants were present in six patients. A higher frequency of a combination of two GLI2 variants (M1352V+D1520N) was found in the study group compared to a reference population (10% vs 0.68%). (Potentially) pathogenic variants were identified in genes associated with midline brain anomalies, including holoprosencephaly, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and absent corpus callosum, and in genes involved in ciliopathies.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusion
AbstractText.content: Combinations of variants in genes associated with midline brain anomalies are frequently present in PSIS and sustain the hypothesis of a polygenic cause of PSIS.
